findings.label: Zero execution-id falls through to key fallback
findings.detail: The fetchLoop predicate `err == nil && route.ExecutionServiceID != 0` treats a legitimate executionServiceId of 0 as a parse miss and routes it via workerIndexForKey(message.Key) instead of the id modulo. Routing stays deterministic so this is not a correctness defect, but if 0 is ever a valid execution id its serialization would key off message.Key rather than the id. Non-blocking; worth a one-line comment.

findings.label: No integration test for the fetchLoop routing/fallback branch
findings.detail: The pure helpers are well unit-tested, but there is no test asserting fetchLoop sends to workerChs[idx], that an executionServiceId:0 value takes the fallback branch, or that shutdown drains per-worker buffers. Reasonably deferred to existing service tests given the live-reader fetchLoop; non-blocking.
